patterns.title: From insight to execution: AI that acts, not advises
patterns.verdict_1line: E05: fourth act — operators published unit economics (UPS 68.5% automated volume / ~28% lower cost per piece; CHR 60% cumulative productivity) and Microsoft disclosed agent revenue run-rates ($450M LinkedIn agentic). All company-reported; audited customer number still missing after five editions. First execution stall logged: in-chat checkout converts ~3x worse than site (S08).
confirmers: audited autonomy or savings percentages in customer (not vendor) case studies
agent revenue disclosures spreading across Q3 vendor earnings
SAP Outbound agent GA confirmation (4th silent edition; drop to background if silent through Q3)
Fabric planning completes GA rollout (5th silent cycle)
weakeners: Q3 earnings calls re-describe 'agents' as 'assistants' — early Q2 reads (Microsoft, C.H. Robinson) show the opposite

patterns.title: The moat is business context, not the model
patterns.verdict_1line: E05: third funded pure-play — Freehand's $75M Series B (spend agents above the systems) joins DeepFabric and Auger. Capital keeps pricing the layer-above thesis; still no published mid-market price list, which is the number that would make build-vs-buy real.
confirmers: 'context layer' appears as its own priced SKU/line item (watch AVEVA+Cognite packaging post-close)
weakeners: frontier models get good enough at raw-table reasoning that definition layers stop mattering (no evidence yet)

patterns.title: AI economics shift from seats to outcomes and tokens
patterns.verdict_1line: E05: two quiet cycles triggered the deep-dive rule; the deliberate pricing sweep ran and the market had moved — SAP CEO (Jul 23 call): per-user pricing 'foolish' for AI-era ERP; Zendesk publishes $1.50/resolution; Epicor sells an ERP agent on outcomes since Sep 2025; Futurum: <1 in 5 buyers prefer per-seat; hybrids dominate. Tell unchanged: Acumatica AI Units terms at 2026 R2.
confirmers: outcome terms appear in mid-market ERP quotes (Acumatica AI Units at 2026 R2 GA is the tell)
weakeners: outcome pricing quietly reverting to consumption floors and minimums — read the fixed/metered/outcome split in every hybrid quote (S13)

patterns.title: Data readiness is the binding constraint
patterns.verdict_1line: E05: consensus found an operator's voice — Dell's CSCO published simplify-standardize-automate ('AI amplifies whatever system it inherits'), the first named operator executive making the constraint argument from inside a major supply chain. Gartner hype cycle (Apr): peak of inflated expectations; 17% deployed vs >60% intent quantifies the same gap.

patterns.title: The plumbing is standardizing: MCP + A2A move from experiment to default
patterns.verdict_1line: E05: CONFIRMER FIRED — the 2026-07-28 final shipped on schedule matching the RC (stateless core, extensions framework, auth hardening, 12-month deprecation policy); four Tier-1 SDKs same-day; day-zero support across major clouds; Honeycomb reports ~20% of interactive queries from agents. Watch moves to who ships first-party connectors next.
confirmers: Acumatica answers with first-party MCP at 2026 R2 (NetSuite set the reference posture)
more operational-stack vendors (WMS, TMS) ship first-party MCP connectors
weakeners: value migrating to proprietary layers on top of the open core

patterns.title: Foundation forecasters are the new baseline — routing and hybrids win
orgs: Academic benchmark wave (2026: volatility, returns, multi-regime)
patterns.verdict_1line: E05: quiet cycle after E04's deep-dive delivered — no new independent benchmarks this week. Standing conclusion holds: credible zero-shot baselines; hybrids and routing win. Quiet-cycle counter: 1 (two triggers the deliberate deep-dive again).
confirmers: planning vendors expose model-routing controls instead of one embedded model
weakeners: a next-gen pre-trained model decisively closes the stable-series gap in independent tests

patterns.title: AI is a demand-side force: the compute buildout moves freight, power and components
patterns.verdict_1line: E05: second corroborated cycle — market microstructure moving: Q2 shipper-forwarder contracts ≤3 months hit 58% (vs 22% a year ago); spot holds ~+38% YoY as Middle East premium fades and AI/semis carry demand; demand side hardened by MSFT's $41B quarterly capex (~$190B calendar-2026 focus). Structural while the buildout runs; fragile if it stalls.
confirmers: Q3 forwarder/carrier earnings quantifying AI-cargo share
pressure spreading to ocean freight or power-constrained warehouse siting
weakeners: an AI investment correction deflating the freight premium (the consultancies' own flagged scenario)

watch_items.item: MCP 2026-07-28 final — RESOLVED E05: shipped on schedule Tue Jul 28 matching the RC (stateless core, MRTR, extensions framework incl. AVEVA + Cognite packaging post-close: does 'context' become its own priced line item (P2 confirmer)? E05: no packaging/pricing news observed this cycle.

Q3 earnings-call language check: do vendors re-describe 'agents' as 'assistants' (P1 weakener)? E05 early reads run the other way — Microsoft discloses agent revenue run-rates; C.H. Robinson holds 'Lean AI'/agents framing through a fourth beat. Full check at Q3 season.

P7 validation: Q3 forwarder/carrier earnings quantifying AI-cargo share; watch spread to ocean freight and power-constrained warehouse siting; weakener = AI capex correction (now openly war-gamed in trade coverage). E05 added: contract windows collapsed to ≤3 months for 58% of new agreements.

Agent-platform pricing: first public mid-market pricing/packaging of DeepFabric-, Auger- or Freehand-class platforms (feeds build-vs-buy math; P1/P2/P3 read). E05: Freehand ($75M Series B) joins the class; still nothing priced publicly.
P6 quiet-cycle counter: 1 (E05). If E06 is also silent, the standing two-quiet-cycles rule triggers the deliberate TSFM deep-dive again — demand/POS-domain benchmark remains the gap.

Cannabis lens: does the 40–60% AI-influenced-transactions projection (E05 S11, trade estimate) get actual measurement? Also standing: do Metrc-class rail owners ship first-party AI vs leaving the layer to specialists?

lessons: Role-play persona must state reader tech fluency explicitly; defaults drift to the builder's level (E01 draft-1 failure).
Glossary (TERMS) and Stack-detail line are template-level; append terms, never strip the layer.
Check publisher families before setting multi:true.
Timeline right-hand markers are third-party forecasts, label as such.

Template Rev E (Jul 3): dual REGISTERS — write exec copy (xone/xwhy) separately from analyst copy for every signal; palette bound to view (warm exec / cool analyst, green brand accent); DELTA object + pattern move chips power the weekly pulse strip; append weekly item to feed.xml; update data-ed numeral; PWA assets (icons/manifest/sw) are permanent — never remove.

Rev F editorial rules (Jul 3): never embed UI pills in running prose; badges nowrap; 62ch reading measures; one green data accent; app icon = approved radar-sweep mark (no redesign/recolor without sign-off); 390px mobile checklist incl. notch clearance runs every edition.

Taxonomy v2 + cannabis lens (Jul 3, Rev G): six locked keys (plan/source/make/deliver/sell/infra); value-chain ribbon + infrastructure foundation band replace filter chips; every research week sweeps all 5 stages + infra + cannabis industry; cann:true signals feed the conditional Industry Lens section (auto-hidden when none qualify); stage-focus line must show honest thin/empty states.

E02 (Jul 9, unattended): mimic-board 'from' links must reference current-edition signal codes — board is edition-scoped (M7-M12), while open_actions in state carries all editions; role-play subagent caught exec-register mechanics leakage in shared 'what' blocks (S12/S13) — shared blocks must pass the exec bar too, since both registers render them.

E03 (Jul 16, unattended): role-play subagents caught (a) date-logic errors in forward-looking copy — check every 'next edition confirms X' claim against the actual calendar (a Jul 23 edition cannot confirm a Jul 28 ship); (b) orphan numbers referencing prior editions ($262B) — attribute cross-edition figures explicitly; (c) internal shorthand (Onematica, SADA) needs TERMS glosses since every edition has potential first-time readers; (d) the scatter caption had a hardcoded signal range (S01-S15) — now genericized, keep it generic; (e) assertions.js still hardcodes 'search stateless finds S12' — keep the MCP-spec card at code S12 (or generalize the assertion when next editing the harness is authorized).

E04 (Jul 23, unattended): role-play caught a WEEKDAY error repeated 6x in the marquee signal (called Jul 28 'Monday'; it is Tuesday) — verify the weekday of every dated claim against a calendar before shipping; date arithmetic ('five days out') can be right while the weekday is wrong.

E04: compile-machinery narration ('this compile ran it', 'surfaced by this week's sweep', 'the card is conservatively single-source') in shared 'what' blocks reads as production mechanics to the exec register — keep provenance honesty, but phrase it in reader terms; detailed provenance lives in the Method box.

E04: TAKES must be business-consequence framed in both registers — an IT-status takeaway ('validate servers against the spec') fails the exec CEO-retell test; the freight-cost story beat it for the third slot. Bare M-code chains (M11 → M3) don't belong in exec-visible surfaces.
E04: P7 added — first pattern-set change; procedure held (E03 candidate flag → multi-source corroboration → Method-box note). Two-cycle candidate rule feels right for pattern additions.

E05 (Jul 30, unattended): the two-quiet-cycles rule fired mid-build (P3) and the resulting deep-dive changed the edition (S13 added after first verification pass). Run the quiet-cycle count during step 0, before research ends — deep-dives belong in the research phase, not the fix loop.

E05: role-play caught a stat quoted with its source's own loose arithmetic ('doubling' for 22%→58%). Recompute every ratio in copy even when the source's framing is being quoted; state the numbers instead of the multiplier when in doubt.

E05: exec-register leakage recurred in shared 'what' blocks on the two most technical cards (S12/S10 first drafts read like release notes). For infrastructure signals, draft the shared 'what' in business language FIRST and push every mechanism to the tech line; the exec bar applies to shared blocks (E02 lesson) and infrastructure cards are where it breaks.
